title: Catch the current before it leaks
story: A lab current source is set to 10 mA, but it is not ideal: a 1 kohm path inside it lets some current leak back. Your sensor needs at least 9 mA flowing through it and at least 0.5 V across it to wake up. Pick the sensor's load resistor.

goals.label: at least 9 mA reaches the sensor
at least 0.5 V across the sensor

hints: The 10 mA splits between the 1 kohm inside and your resistor, like a current divider.
Load current = 10 mA * 1000 / (1000 + R). For 9 mA you need R of about 111 ohm or less.
Voltage = load current * R. Too small a resistor gives almost all the current but almost no voltage.
